title: Global Human-guided Counterfactual Explanations for Molecular Properties via Reinforcement Learning

problem.claim: Global counterfactual explanations for molecular property prediction should explain high-level model and data properties while remaining interpretable to domain experts.

gap.claim: Evaluation of global counterfactual explanations is difficult because real-world datasets lack human-annotated ground truth, and increasing dataset scale challenges random search-based methods.

contributions.claim: RLHEX is a global explanation model for molecular property prediction that aligns counterfactual explanations with human-defined principles.
RLHEX combines a VAE-based graph generator with an adapter that adjusts latent representations to human-defined principles, and uses PPO for optimization.
The authors release code and data for RLHEX.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors describe RLHEX as a novel global explanation model for molecular property prediction.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Across three molecular datasets, RLHEX covered 4.12% more input graphs and reduced the average distance between the counterfactual explanation set and the input set by 0.47%.

narrative_sequence.summary: Counterfactual explanations can help understand graph-based neural networks, while global explanations are desirable for explaining high-level model and data properties.
Lack of human-annotated ground truth makes global counterfactual explanations difficult to evaluate, and large datasets challenge random search methods.
The paper introduces RLHEX, which aligns molecular counterfactual explanations with human-defined principles using a VAE-based graph generator, a latent-space adapter, and PPO.
The authors report improved input-graph coverage and reduced distance to the input set across three molecular datasets.
The authors state that RLHEX provides a flexible framework for incorporating different human-designed principles and release code and data.

source_observation.claim: Aligning counterfactual explanations with human-defined principles is presented as a way to improve interpretability and expert evaluation.

interpretation.claim: Explanation systems may benefit from incorporating domain-specific principles into their generation process.

application.claim: When designing explanations for specialized domains, expose mechanisms for encoding expert-defined principles.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether the human-defined principles generalize across domains or improve expert judgments in independent evaluations.

source_observation.claim: The reported method combines a graph generator, latent-space adaptation, and reinforcement-learning optimization to address large-scale global explanation generation.

interpretation.claim: Structured generation and optimization may be useful when random search becomes difficult at dataset scale.

application.claim: For large graph explanation spaces, consider generative models with constrained latent representations and policy optimization.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify comparisons with random search or other baselines, nor the conditions under which the reported gains hold.

unknowns: The three molecular datasets are not identified.
Baselines, evaluation protocols, and statistical uncertainty are not reported.
The specific human-defined principles and their expert-evaluation procedures are not described.
The abstract does not establish independent verification of the reported results.
